title: Electricity: Resistivity, Circuits and EMF
seo_title: Year 12 A Level Physics: Electricity Worksheets
standard_text: Current, potential difference and resistance, resistivity, circuits with series and parallel resistors, energy and power, potential dividers, electromotive force and internal resistance.
meta_desc: Free Year 12 A level physics worksheets on electricity: charge and current, resistance and resistivity, series and parallel circuits, power, potential dividers, e.m.f. and internal resistance. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

Current is the rate of flow of charge, I = ΔQ/Δt; potential difference is energy per unit charge, V = W/Q. Resistance R = V/I, and for a wire R = ρL/A.

Series: R = R₁ + R₂. Parallel: 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂. A real cell has internal resistance: ε = I(R + r), and the terminal p.d. is ε − Ir.

Example

6 Ω and 3 Ω in parallel?

1/R = 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2

Answer: 2 Ω

Example

ε = 6.0 V, r = 0.5 Ω, R = 5.5 Ω. Current?

I = 6.0 ÷ (5.5 + 0.5)

Answer: 1.0 A

Common mistakes

  • Adding parallel resistances.
  • Using the diameter in A = πr².
  • Forgetting the internal resistance when finding the current.

faq.a: ρ = RA/L, a property of the material (unit Ω m), not of one particular wire.
The p.d. across the internal resistance of a cell, Ir. The terminal p.d. is ε − Ir.
